units.text: Many students believe that they need a special talent to learn English. In fact, a daily habit matters much more. If you read one page and learn five words every day, you will improve faster than someone who studies for five hours once a week. It is also important not to be afraid of a mistake: each one shows you what to practise next. After a few months you will notice real progress, and you will feel more confident when you speak in class or write an essay.

units.text: Online lessons have become a normal part of school life. Their main advantage is clear: a student in a small village can get access to the same teachers as a student in the capital. Messages, games and videos distract young people, and nobody checks whether they are listening. For this reason, online study works best for students who can plan their own time.

units.text: As a city grows, its streets fill with cars. In the morning the traffic moves so slowly that a short commute to school can take an hour. Cars are also a major cause of air pollution, which is harmful for everyone who lives nearby. Many cities try to reduce the problem by improving public transport. New metro lines and bus lanes carry thousands of people quickly. When more people leave their cars at home, the streets become quieter, the air becomes cleaner and everybody saves time.

Farms consume the largest share, but families can help too. A tap with a small leak loses many litres every day, so it should be repaired quickly. Taking shorter showers and watering the garden in the evening also make a difference. If each of us changes one small habit, we can protect our rivers for the next generation.

Doctors therefore advise a regular routine: go to bed and get up at the same time, and put your phone away an hour before you sleep.

units.text: When Dilnoza's class was invited to a weekend clean-up of the riverbank, she was reluctant at first. Everyone could contribute in a different way, by collecting litter, carrying heavy bags or making tea for the others. Dilnoza agreed to come, but only once. By lunchtime, however, the bank looked completely different, and she found the work far more rewarding than she had expected. Now she goes every month. It is a real commitment, she admits, but she has never regretted it.

He is ambitious: he wants to study engineering at a strong university and one day design bridges. However, his family cannot pay high fees, so a scholarship is his first priority. Every evening he compares universities online. He writes down each entry requirement, such as a test score, a language certificate or a date for applications, and marks the ones he can already meet. Some of his choices are far from home, and his mother worries about that. Timur knows that his list will change many times. Still, he believes that if he plans carefully and keeps working, he will eventually find a place that fits both his dreams and his budget.

After two months the owner said that Jasur was the most reliable worker she had ever had: he was never late and never forgot a task. Before the summer ended, he even managed to negotiate higher pay for weekend work. Most of all, he learnt how to plan his time.

units.text: For the school science fair, Shahzoda and her partner decided to investigate a simple question: does music help plants grow? They planted twelve bean seeds in identical pots and placed them by the same window. Six pots heard quiet music for an hour every day, and six did not. Before they started, Shahzoda predicted that the plants with music would grow faster. Every morning the girls measured each plant with a ruler and wrote the numbers in a notebook, because they wanted their results to be accurate. After four weeks, both groups were almost the same height. The girls had no evidence that music made a difference, so their conclusion was honest: in their test, it did not. The judges liked their careful method and gave them second prize.

units.text: Last week a message appeared in the class group chat: the summer holidays would start two weeks early. Within an hour, the rumour had spread to every class in the school, and some pupils were already planning trips. Nilufar was not so sure. The message had a dramatic headline in capital letters, but it gave no names, no dates and no link to the school's website. She asked herself one simple question: what is the source of this story? When she checked the school's own page, there was nothing about the holidays. The next morning the head teacher explained that the message was misleading and had started as a joke. Since then, Nilufar has followed one rule: before she shares any news, she checks where it comes from.

units.text: In many urban areas, every free piece of land is used for new buildings. In Rustam's neighbourhood, however, the residents decided to save a small empty yard between two blocks of flats. Together they planted young trees, built wooden benches and laid a path for prams and bicycles. Three years later, the yard has become a real garden. In July, when the streets are burning hot, older people sit in the shade and children play there until late. The benefit is not only cooler air: neighbours who never spoke before now know each other's names. Of course, a garden needs constant care. Every family takes turns to water the trees and maintain the benches, and nobody needs to be told twice.
